subject: Edit or Reprint plots in Excel

messages.author: 1ec3f8d9a5847ab4
messages.subject: Edit or Reprint plots in Excel
parts:
Dear Phil,

first things first: I'm currently working with your packages mirt and mirtCAT for my PhD and I'm immensely thankful for your great work!

While I got quite font of R during the last months, I'm still building and editing my tables and figures in Excel. Yet with the (item-)plots I'm not getting any further with this method. Is there any possibility to extract the information out of mirt / R in order to rebuild or edit the mirt-plots in Excel?

For example I've plotted a joint Item Information Trace Lines figure with this code:
---
colors <- c("#17365c","#2e4a6c", "#455e7d", "#5d728d", "#74869d", "#8b9bae",      "#a2afbe", "#b9c3ce", "#d1d7de", "#a2a2a2", "#8b8b8b", "#747474", "#5c5c5c") 

theme <- simpleTheme(lty= 1:7, col.line = colors)

plot(model, type = 'infotrace', which.items = 1:14, facet_items = FALSE, auto.key=list(points=FALSE, lines=TRUE, space = "right"), par.settings=theme)
---

Since I want to compare 14 Items it got somewhat messy (see attachment). I would like to rebuild it in Excel in order to better differentiate the curves etc. Btw: I know of the possibility to divide the plots by setting facet_items = TRUE, but would prefer all lines in the same plot. It's only an especially complex example really. Same will be my challenge for other (and easier) types of mirt-plots, too, as all figures should have the same style in the end.

If you have any solution or idea that would be very helpful to me!

Best wishes
Nick

messages.author: 1ec3f8d9a5847ab4
messages.subject: Re: Edit or Reprint plots in Excel
parts:
As I found the function iteminfo() in the mirt-documentary I just realized how to do what I wanted. Just in case anyone having the same issue, here is my solution:

The iteminfo() function gives you the item information-value for any specific theta. So I wrote a function that extracts a lot of theta values in a sequence for every item in a unidimensional mirt-model and copies it to an excel-sheet. You will need the xlsx-package for this.

CODE:
-----
install.packages("xlsx")
library(xlsx)

infoplot.to.xlsx <- function (model, path) { #the function needs a mirt-model as input as well as a path (string) in order to tell it where to save the xlsx
  thetas <- seq(-6, 6, 0.01) #creates a sequence of theta-values with 0.01 steps. I found that quite detailed, but you could alter that if you want.
  sheet <- cbind(thetas)
  
  for (i in 1:model@Data[["nitems"]]) {
    item <- extract.item(model, i)
    info <- iteminfo(item, Theta = thetas)
    sheet <- cbind(sheet, info)
  }
  
  sheet <- as.data.frame(sheet)
  names(sheet) <- c("Theta", paste("Item", 1:model@Data[["nitems"]], sep = "")) #renames the columns, so in your excel sheet you will now which column is which item...
  write.xlsx(sheet, file = path, sheetName = substitute(model))
  
}
-----

As I'm not much of a developer/programmer, I'm not quite sure if that's the best way to do it, but it worked for me. You get an xlsx-file, in which you can build and edit a custom linear-diagram from the extracted data. The results looked quite similar to the R-plot, so I think it's a valid way to do. Yet maybe Phil can confirm that or tell a better way to do :)

Stay healthy
Nick
